title: Soong Modules, Products, Flags, and APEX Boundaries

scout.purpose: Master soong modules, products, flags, and apex boundaries through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend soong modules, products, flags, and apex boundaries.

blocks.text: Soong reads Android.bp blueprint declarations and builds a typed dependency graph executed through generated Ninja work. Modules declare sources, libraries, visibility, install destinations, apex availability, licenses, tests, and target or product variations. Defaults reduce repetition but can obscure ownership when overused. Product configuration selects packages, properties, overlays, partitions, and release flags. A module compiling does not prove it is installed in the chosen product or available across a partition boundary.

blocks.text: Use explicit visibility and dependency direction. Platform, system_ext, product, vendor, and APEX boundaries carry compatibility and update consequences. APEX packages can update selected system components independently and constrain what code or APIs are available. Feature launch flags isolate untested behavior; build flags shape products but should not substitute for stable runtime compatibility. Avoid environment reads and ad hoc genrules when typed modules express inputs and outputs. Keep generated artifacts deterministic.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Inspect module-info, dependency queries, installed-files lists, Ninja commands, and target output. Change one module input and verify incremental scope. Test host and device modules, product variants, clean and incremental builds, APEX packaging, license metadata, and visibility denial. When migrating Make, compare semantics rather than transliterating lines. Platform changes need owners, reproducibility, presubmit tests, image size, boot, compatibility, and rollback evidence.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

trap_check.mistake: Adding a module to Android.bp compiles it only when selected by the graph; it does not automatically install it in every product image.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Add a typed Soong library and test, wire one product intentionally, inspect variants and install output, and verify incremental, visibility, license, and image effects.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: What decides whether a built module is present on a product?
recall.answer: Product and dependency selection plus install and partition properties, not merely the existence of its Android.bp declaration.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
